strings.school_scene.p2.changing_friendship.summ: Tara Das has been slipping away before dismissal on Thursdays to collect her younger sibling from the primary gate before maidan running practice.
strings.school_scene.p2.changing_friendship.tiff: During tiffin break in the courtyard, Tara checks her watch twice and folds a primary-school gate slip into her grammar notebook before looking up at you.
Ask quietly whether the Thursday afternoon timing is getting too tight to manage alone.
Tara admits she has been sprinting between the last bell and the primary gate so her younger brother is not left waiting outside before her maidan run.
Tell Tara you will check your own Thursday evening timings at home before promising anything.
Tara appreciates that you do not overpromise on the spot; you agree to check your household evening schedule first.
Tell Tara you will speak with the care worker before the afternoon handover about a Thursday detour.
Tara nods gratefully as you plan to check the care home afternoon sign-in book before making a commitment.
Wish her well for afternoon practice and leave the folded gate slip private.
You keep the tiffin conversation light and unpressured; Tara thanks you for sitting with her before the bell.
strings.school_scene.p2.changing_friendship.fami: At home in the evening, your household adult goes over the week's market and study timings while you mention Tara's Thursday afternoon pickup.
Move your Thursday household errand twenty minutes later so you can walk the primary-gate stretch after dismissal.
Your household adult agrees to shift the Thursday errand window, provided you are back at the desk before evening revision.
Keep your Thursday household hours unchanged so evening study stays predictable.
Your household adult respects your call to keep Thursday evenings steady and unhurried.
strings.school_scene.p2.changing_friendship.care: Logging a Thursday Detour at the Care Home
At the care home staff desk before the 15:00 shift handover, the care worker checks the afternoon return ledger as you explain the Thursday detour.
Write a Thursday 16:30 return note in the handover book for the evening staff.
The care worker logs the twenty-minute Thursday detour in the handover book so the evening staff know exactly when to expect you.
Keep your usual post-dismissal return time in the sign-in book.
The care worker keeps your standard return entry unchanged without any fuss.
strings.school_scene.p2.changing_friendship.beng: A Note Passed After Bengali Period
As sixth-period Bengali wraps up in the Class XI Humanities room, Tara slides a pencilled timetable across the bench showing the fifteen-minute overlap on Thursdays.
Offer to walk the primary-school pickup leg with her on Thursdays so neither of you misses class.
Tara's shoulders drop in relief; splitting the walk means she can stay through the final bell and still make her maidan warm-up.
Go together to Amrita Basu to request an official Thursday dismissal pass.
Amrita Basu listens carefully, notes the sibling pickup in the class register, and issues an official Thursday gate pass.
Be honest that your own afternoon commitments do not leave room to cover the Thursday run.
Tara thanks you for telling her plainly ahead of time instead of cancelling at the last minute.
strings.school_scene.p2.changing_friendship.gate: At the School Gate After Dismissal
Outside the courtyard after the 15:50 dismissal bell, Tara adjusts her satchel strap as the primary-school lane begins to fill.
Walk the primary-school lane together and hand her brother off before the maidan turn.
With the two of you sharing the walk, the pickup finishes ten minutes early and the Thursday routine settles into an easy rhythm.
Stop by Amrita Basu's desk at the gate to confirm the standing Thursday arrangement.
Amrita Basu signs off on the standing Thursday arrangement so Tara never has to slip out anxiously again.
Let Tara know you can only manage today's walk and need to keep future Thursdays free.
Tara thanks you warmly for helping today and parts on good terms at the lane corner.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.title: A Useful Group Project
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.summary: Amrita Basu assigns a cross-section practical and chart folder pairing lab observations from Ishan Sheikh and Deven Chakraborty with clean tabular layouts from Mira Sen.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.briefing.p: In the Class XI Science room during the chemistry block, Amrita Basu lays out the half-yearly practical chart rubric while Ishan Sheikh and Deven Chakraborty compare apparatus logs.
Divide the observation tables with Deven and Ishan right away so each bench has a clear role.
Deven marks the measurement columns while Ishan logs the trial timings, giving the group a clean starting ledger.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.briefing.f: Check at home this evening whether the dining table can be cleared for drafting the large chart sheets.
You note down the chart dimensions to check with your household adult before promising evening drafting space.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.briefing.c: Ask at the care home this evening to reserve the common-room study table for chart ruling.
You jot down the evening hours to coordinate the care home common-room table before taking the chart sheets.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.briefing.r: Opt for the individual observation logbook so your schedule stays independent.
Amrita Basu records your choice of the solo logbook without penalty, and Deven wishes you well with the readings.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.family_dra: Clearing the Evening Table at Home
At home after supper, you unroll the Bristol board sheets while your household adult checks how long the table will be needed.
Rule the baseline axes tonight and pack the ink pens neatly before 20:00.
Your household adult clears the end of the table for an hour, leaving the group's chart grid crisp and ready for class.
Keep the household table free tonight and leave the chart ruling for school hours.
You roll the Bristol board back into its tube so the household evening stays uncluttered.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.care_draft: In the care home study room at 19:00, the evening rota leaves one wide table open beside the stationery cupboard.
Book the corner of the common-room table for forty minutes to rule the group's chart grid.
With the table reserved in the evening study log, you finish the ruled layout cleanly before lights-down.
Leave the common-room table open for the younger residents and keep your evening quiet.
You leave the wide table free for the floor and pack your folder neatly for tomorrow.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.handover.p: At the start of fourth-period English, Mira Sen checks the ruled margins on the borrowed observation packet before the afternoon stationery shift.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.handover.r: Return the completed observation packet to Mira on the bell with every column checked.
Mira checks off the columns with a relieved smile, noting that the packet came back cleaner than she lent it.
Offer to stay after dismissal with Ishan and Deven to reconcile the mismatched second-trial readings.
Mira marks the two discrepant rows in pencil so you, Ishan and Deven can work through the maths together after last bell.
Hand in your own completed section now and step back from the extra after-school session.
Deven and Mira file your completed section into the folder and thank you for delivering your share on time.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.review.tit: Working Through the Readings After Dismissal
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.review.pro: In Room XI-A after the 15:50 bell, Deven Chakraborty and Ishan Sheikh spread the trial sheets across the front bench.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.review.exp: Walk through the unit conversion step by step until all three of you can explain the curve.
By the time you pack up, Deven and Ishan have both mastered the derivation and the group folder is ready for Amrita Basu.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.review.ret: Leave the corrected summary table with Ishan so the folder is complete before the gate closes.
Ishan clips the corrected summary sheet into the binder and thanks you for keeping the packet on schedule.
strings.school_scene.p2.group_project.review.ref: Wrap up your part on the bell so you can head home before evening obligations.
Deven nods understandingly and packs the remaining rough sheets so you can head out on time.
strings.school_scene.p2.household_responsibility: A Renegotiated Household Responsibility
As Class XI unit tests approach, evening errands and rota duties collide with peak revision hours until you renegotiate a fairer schedule.
First-Period Revision Timetable Notice
During second-period Physics in the Class XI Science room, Amrita Basu writes the recommended 18:30-20:00 problem-practice block on the board—right across your usual evening duty hour.
Plan to sit down with your household adult tonight to renegotiate the evening errand hour.
You copy the unit-test revision timetable into your diary so you can show your household adult the exact overlap tonight.
Plan to speak with the care worker during afternoon handover about shifting your evening rota slot.
You copy the unit-test revision hours clearly so the care worker can review the evening rota before shift change.
Keep your current evening duty hours as they are and fit revision into the remaining gaps.
You decide not to reopen the evening schedule right now and keep your existing routine steady.
Renegotiating the Evening Errand at Home
At home at 18:15, your household adult sets the market bag by the door while you open your school diary to the unit-test timetable.
Propose shifting the market errand to right after school so the 18:30-20:00 study block stays unbroken.
Your household adult agrees to the earlier errand slot, giving you an uninterrupted ninety-minute revision block every evening.
Propose alternating the evening errand days so you have three full study evenings each week.
Your household adult agrees to split the weekday errands, freeing Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday evenings for revision.
Drop the request for now and carry out tonight's errand on the old schedule.
You take the market list without argument, keeping the household routine unchanged for now.
Reviewing the Evening Rota at Handover
At the care home staff desk at 14:15, the care worker opens the weekly resident duty ledger beside the handover clipboard.
Ask to move your dining-hall clear-up turn to the 17:30 slot so the 18:30 study hour is protected.
The care worker updates the duty ledger and leaves a handover note for the evening staff confirming your new 17:30 slot.
Arrange to alternate the evening rota turn with another senior resident during unit-test weeks.
The care worker records the alternating rota in the handover book so your study evenings stay balanced.
Leave your current evening rota slot as written in the ledger.
The care worker closes the ledger kindly and reminds you that the rota can always be revisited before exams.
Settling into the Evening Study Hour
At 19:30, Ishan Sheikh checks the worked physics problems with you over the evening revision checklist.
Confirm the redesigned early-errand timetable with Amrita Basu and Ishan for the rest of term.
With the duty hour moved ahead of supper, your evening study block runs without interruption and the new rota holds firm.
Confirm the alternating weekday duty schedule so both obligations and revision stay covered.
Sharing the weekday turns keeps the household running smoothly while giving you steady revision nights.
Step back to your original evening hours rather than locking in the new timetable.
Ishan notes your preferred timing without complaint, and you keep your evenings flexible.

strings.conversation.amrita_basu.greeting: Amrita Basu looks up from the Class XI attendance register with a measured, attentive nod.
strings.conversation.tara_das.greeting: Tara Das balances her notebook against her satchel, keeping one eye on the courtyard clock.
strings.conversation.ishan_sheikh.greeting: Ishan Sheikh flips open his pocket notebook where practical readings sit beside neighbourhood bus notes.
strings.conversation.deven_chakraborty.greeting: Deven Chakraborty straightens the brass callipers on the bench and checks the group's chart ruler.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.title: A New Benchmate from Another District
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.summary: Deven Chakraborty transfers into the Class XI section mid-term from another district and tries to bridge a three-week syllabus gap before the first unit test.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.arrival.titl: A New Name on the Morning Register
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.arrival.prom: At the start of first-period Mathematics in the Class XI Science room, Amrita Basu introduces Deven Chakraborty, newly transferred from Burdwan with a half-filled syllabus notebook, and looks along the middle benches for a spare space.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.arrival.shar: Slide your bag over to share the bench with Deven and open your chapter index.
Deven sits down with a quiet nod of relief and marks the three topics his previous school had not yet reached.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.arrival.fami: Check at home tonight whether you can pack your first-month rough notebooks for Deven to borrow.
You jot down the missing chapter numbers to check against your shelf at home this evening.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.arrival.care: Check at the care home tonight whether you can use the evening study desk to copy out the chapter summary.
You note the missing exercise numbers to copy at the care home common-room table tonight.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.arrival.refu: Give Deven a polite nod and keep your bench space as it is so you can focus on today's exercise.
Ishan Sheikh makes room on the next bench over, and the mathematics lesson continues smoothly.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.family.title: Sorting Spare Notebooks at Home
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.family.promp: At home after tea, your household adult watches you pull April's rough exercise books from the lower shelf while you explain the new student's mid-term transfer.
Clip your April worked sheets into a spare folder so Deven can take them over tiffin tomorrow.
Your household adult hands you a brown paper cover and two brass clips so the pages stay tidy in your satchel.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.family.refus: Keep your rough books on the home shelf so you do not misplace them before unit tests.
Your household adult agrees it is sensible to keep your own revision shelf complete before the test week.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.care.title: Copying Summary Sheets in the Common Room
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.care.prompt: In the care home study room at 18:30, the care worker checks the stationery drawer while you mention the transfer student in your section.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.care.book.la: Spend twenty minutes copying out the first three chapter outlines onto ruled foolscap for Deven.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.care.book.ou: The care worker sets out two clean foolscap sheets and a paperclip so the summary packet is ready for tomorrow's tiffin break.
Keep your evening study slot strictly for your own unit-test preparation.
The care worker nods approvingly as you settle into your own physics problems without distraction.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.tiffin.title: Comparing Syllabuses at Tiffin
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.tiffin.promp: By the courtyard wall during tiffin, Deven Chakraborty compares his transfer syllabus against Mira Sen's neat index while Ishan Sheikh points out which derivations Amrita Basu emphasises.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.tiffin.retur: Hand Deven the completed chapter outline and collect your clipped index sheet on the bell.
Deven copies the topic sequence cleanly before the bell and hands your folder back with every page in order.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.tiffin.catch: Offer to stay thirty minutes after dismissal with Ishan and Deven to walk through the missed derivations.
Deven and Ishan mark the two trickiest theorems in pencil so the three of you can tackle them at the last bell.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.tiffin.refus: Wish Deven luck with the reading list and keep the rest of your tiffin break unhurried.
Mira Sen lends Deven her spare syllabus slip, and you enjoy the remaining tiffin minutes in the courtyard shade.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.catchup.titl: Thirty Minutes at the Blackboard After Bell
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.catchup.prom: In Room XI-A after the 15:50 dismissal bell, Ishan Sheikh chalks the first trigonometric identity on the corner of the board while Deven opens his new exercise book.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.catchup.expl: Work through the two missed proofs together until Deven can solve the third example on his own.
When Deven finishes the third proof without checking the margin, the awkwardness of being the new transfer student finally melts away.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.catchup.retu: Check that Mira's borrowed index sheet is tucked back into the class folder before locking up.
Mira collects her index sheet at the door with a grateful nod, and Deven packs his updated notes for home.
strings.school_scene.p2.new_student.catchup.refu: Pack your satchel on the bell and leave Ishan and Deven to finish the board work.
Ishan waves you off cheerfully and stays behind to finish the example with Deven.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.title: The Cracked 250 ml Beaker
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.summary: A borosilicate laboratory beaker slips against the stone sink during practical work, leaving the bench partners to decide how to face the breakage register.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.lab.title: A Sharp Clink at the Lab Sink
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.lab.prompt: Near the end of fifth-period practicals in the science lab, a soapy 250 ml beaker slips from the wet clamp between you and Deven Chakraborty, cracking cleanly across the spout in the stone sink before anyone at the front desk turns around.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.lab.talk.l: Speak quietly with Deven at the bench about logging the cracked beaker together before chemistry tomorrow.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.lab.talk.o: Deven admits he tightened the wet clamp in a hurry and is relieved you are willing to face the register together rather than pointing fingers.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.lab.family: Check at home tonight whether your household can cover half the small breakage deposit if required.
You wrap the cracked glass safely in brown paper by the sink tray and plan to speak with your household adult tonight.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.lab.care.l: Speak with the care worker before afternoon handover about counter-signing a school lab breakage slip.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.lab.care.o: You set the cracked beaker safely in the wash tray and plan to check the care home stationery procedure at handover.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.lab.refuse: Place the cracked glass in the disposal tray without getting drawn into who pays the deposit.
You clear the sink safely and return to writing up your own observation table while Deven quietly notes the breakage himself.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.family.tit: Mentioning the Lab Breakage at Home
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.family.pro: At home in the evening, you explain the cracked 250 ml beaker at the shared bench while your household adult checks the monthly school expense envelope.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.family.agr: Set aside your half of the small apparatus replacement fee so neither bench partner carries it alone.
Your household adult appreciates your honesty and tucks the exact change into a small envelope for the school office.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.family.ref: Leave the household expense envelope untouched until the teacher asks for a formal slip.
Your household adult agrees to wait and see what Amrita Basu writes in the apparatus register first.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.care.title: Checking the Breakage Slip at Handover
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.care.promp: At the care home desk before the 15:00 shift change, you explain the cracked laboratory beaker to the care worker on duty.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.care.agree: Ask the care worker for a counter-signed institutional note explaining the shared bench accident.
The care worker thanks you for speaking up promptly and signs a neat note for the school science stock book.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.care.refus: Hold off on requesting an official care-home note unless the school demands a replacement fee.
The care worker makes a pencilled memo on the desk pad and leaves the formal voucher book closed for now.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.register.p: At the start of third-period Chemistry in the Class XI Science room, Amrita Basu opens the hardbound apparatus register and asks Bench Three to account for the cracked 250 ml beaker found in the sink tray.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.register.s: Step up beside Deven so both names go down together on the bench maintenance entry.
Amrita Basu notes that you both owned up without excuses and assigns a short apparatus-cupboard tally after school instead of a fine.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.register.a: Show Amrita Basu the worn rubber sleeve on the clamp and ask for it to be logged as routine wear.
Amrita Basu inspects the perished clamp sleeve, marks the beaker down as normal laboratory wear-and-tear, and waives the deposit.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.register.r: Stay at your seat and let Deven explain his own grip on the clamp.
Deven explains the slip calmly at the front desk; Amrita Basu records the note without lecturing the class.
strings.school_scene.p2.broken_beaker.after_scho: Tallying the Glassware Cupboard After Dismissal
In the courtyard outside the science room after the 15:50 bell, Ishan Sheikh holds the stock checklist while Deven brings out the crate of replacement rubber clamp sleeves.
Fit the new rubber sleeves onto the clamps with Deven so the bench glassware is safer for everyone.
In twenty minutes the clamps are refitted, the glassware shelf is tallied, and Deven thanks you for standing by him.
Bring the completed glassware tally to Amrita Basu's table for her closing signature.
Amrita Basu initials the stock book with a warm nod, closing the matter cleanly for the term.
Head home now that your name is signed in the register and leave the shelf sorting for tomorrow.
Ishan and Deven lock up the cupboard before the gate closes and part with you on easy terms.

strings.school_scene.p2.football_or_coaching.sum: The Class XI inter-section football practice on Banyan Maidan lands across the same late-afternoon hour as your evening coaching and revision batch.

Tell Tara you will speak with your household adult tonight about shifting your coaching batch hours.
You copy down the maidan practice timings to go over with your household adult after supper.
Tell Tara you will speak with the care worker at handover about balancing maidan practice and evening prep.
You note down the Tuesday-Thursday maidan hours to review at the care home desk before 15:00.
Pass on the football squad list this term so your evening study batch stays uninterrupted.

At home at 18:20, your household adult looks over the coaching tutor's weekday schedule beside the school's Banyan Maidan practice slip.
Propose switching your weekday coaching slot to the Saturday morning consolidated batch.
Your household adult agrees to the Saturday batch swap, provided you sit down to revise promptly at 19:00 on practice days.
Propose attending Tuesday football practice and Thursday coaching while sharing notes with Ishan.

Ask to move your evening revision sign-in to the 19:00–21:00 block on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
The care worker logs the later prep block in the handover book so you can play full maidan sessions twice a week.
Arrange to attend one maidan session a week and swap evening coaching problem sheets with Ishan.
The care worker notes the one-day sports pass in the ledger, keeping the rest of your week anchored to study.

strings.school_scene.p2.football_or_coaching.bal: Settling the Evening Timetable After Practice
At 19:30 in the evening study space, Ishan Sheikh passes over the coaching practice sheet while your boots dry by the door.
Confirm the shifted weekend coaching batch with Amrita Basu and Ishan for the rest of term.
With the batch moved to Saturday morning, your weekday evenings hold space for both the maidan eleven and quiet revision.
Lock in the alternating Tuesday-Thursday arrangement with Tara Das and Ishan.

strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.title: Two Red Lines on the Half-Yearly Script
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.summary: Your half-yearly answer script comes back with marks deducted for a valid alternate working method, leaving you to weigh a calm review request with Amrita Basu.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.script.title: Scripts Returned in Fourth Period
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.script.promp: During fourth-period English in the Class XI Commerce room, the bundled half-yearly answer scripts are handed back; on Question 4, your final answer matches the key, but three step-marks are crossed out in red ink beside an unfamiliar shorthand note.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.script.compa: Compare your step-by-step working quietly with Mira Sen's full-mark script before the bell.
Mira points out that you used the substitution method from the reference text rather than the board shorthand, which explains why the fast-marking pass missed the middle line.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.script.famil: Take the script home tonight to get your household adult's signature and advice before raising a query.
You slip the marked script flat into your folder to review at home this evening.
Bring the script to the care worker before afternoon handover to discuss whether to attach a re-total note.
You place the marked script carefully in your satchel to go over at the care home desk.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.script.refus: Accept the mark as written and tuck the script away rather than reopening the grading.
You note the preferred board method in your margin for next time and move on with the lesson.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.family.title: Going Over the Answer Script at Home
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.family.promp: At home at 19:00, your household adult puts on reading glasses to examine Question 4 alongside the textbook example.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.family.query: Write a polite two-line re-total request in the guardian margin asking for the alternate steps to be checked.
Your household adult signs beneath the calm, factual note so you can show it to Amrita Basu tomorrow.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.family.refus: Ask your household adult to sign the script without a query so the matter is closed.
Your household adult signs the top corner cleanly and reminds you that three marks in Term 1 will not define the year.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.care.title: Reviewing the Script Margin at Handover
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.care.prompt: At the care home desk at 14:05, the care worker looks over your half-yearly paper before signing the guardian acknowledgement line.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.care.query.l: Draft a respectful note on the guardian line asking for a step-mark review on Question 4.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.care.query.o: The care worker counter-signs your clear, polite query note and commends you for checking the textbook first.
Have the care worker sign the acknowledgement line without attaching a mark query.
The care worker signs the paper warmly and records your half-yearly score in the house progress book.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.tiffin.title: Checking the Marking Scheme at Tiffin
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.tiffin.promp: In the courtyard during tiffin, Ishan Sheikh and Mira Sen hold the pinned model answer sheet while you check how the intermediate steps were weighted.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.tiffin.retur: Return Mira's borrowed model script on the bell and keep the annotated copy for your own revision.
Mira tucks her script back into her file and thanks you for keeping the pages uncreased.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.tiffin.revie: Put your name down for Amrita Basu's ten-minute script review window after dismissal.
Ishan walks with you to the staffroom noticeboard, where you pencil your roll number into the after-school review column.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.tiffin.refus: Decide that understanding the marking scheme is enough and skip the after-school review queue.
Ishan nods sensibly; knowing what the examiners want for the annual paper is already half the battle.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.review.title: Script Review at the Front Desk
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.review.promp: In Room XI-A after the 15:50 bell, Amrita Basu sets her red pen beside the register and invites you to walk through your working on Question 4.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.review.expla: Point calmly to the substitution line in the textbook and explain how your third step reaches the same line.
Amrita Basu follows the algebra line by line, restores two of the three marks in the register, and shows you why the final unit statement still needed one explicit line.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.review.retur: Thank Amrita Basu for re-totalling the page and return the checked script to the class bundle.
Amrita Basu updates the mark column cleanly and files your script back into the section bundle without any stiffness.
strings.school_scene.p2.unfair_mark.review.refus: Thank her for explaining the rubric and withdraw the re-marking request so the bundle can close.
Amrita Basu appreciates your maturity and marks down a reminder to accept both textbook methods on the next test.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.title: An Unfinished Exercise Book Before the Bell
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.summary: Ten minutes before the physics homework register, a classmate asks to copy your worked numericals verbatim, forcing a choice between lending answers, teaching the method, or keeping your book closed.
A Whispered Request in Second Period

At the start of second-period Physics in the Class XI Science room, Ishan Sheikh opens a half-blank exercise book—last night's bus breakdown delayed his return—and asks whether he can copy your final three numericals before Amrita Basu calls the row.
Show him only the rough formula setup in pencil so he works the arithmetic himself.
Ishan copies the starting equations quickly and calculates his own figures rather than transcribing yours word for word.
Tell Ishan you will draft a clean formula-hint sheet at home tonight so nobody is scrambling before class.
Ishan owns up to the two unfinished problems today and agrees to use your hint sheet before the next set.
Tell Ishan you will write out a worked hint card at the care home desk tonight for the bench.
Ishan accepts a partial mark on today's homework and looks forward to working from the hint card tomorrow.
Keep your exercise book closed in your satchel and say plainly that identical working will get both books flagged.
Ishan winces but admits you are right about Amrita Basu's eye for identical lines, and hands in what he finished honestly.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.family.t: Drafting a Formula Hint Card at Home
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.family.p: At home at 18:30, your household adult brings a cup of cha to the table while you rule a separate index card showing the physics formulas without the final answers.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.family.h: Write out the step-by-step hints without numerical answers so classmates can solve the set fairly.
Your household adult nods approvingly at the distinction between helping a friend learn and handing over finished work.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.family.r: Set the extra card aside and focus strictly on your own homework book tonight.
You finish your own problem set early and pack your bag with plenty of time to spare.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.care.tit: Writing a Hint Sheet in the Care Home Study Room
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.care.pro: In the care home common room at 18:30, the care worker pauses by your bench as you copy the free-body diagram hints onto a spare slip.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.care.hin: Prepare a diagram-and-formula slip that leaves the final substitution for the reader to complete.
The care worker praises the clear boundary: useful enough to unblock a friend, honest enough for any teacher to inspect.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.care.ref: Keep your study hour for your own notebook and leave the shared slip unwritten.
You complete your own exercises neatly before the dinner bell.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.tiffin.p: During tiffin break in the courtyard, Deven Chakraborty notices two benches comparing homework margins before the afternoon monitor collects the stack.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.tiffin.r: Collect your rough formula sheet from Ishan before the homework stack goes to the staffroom.
Ishan hands back your rough sheet intact and shows you the last two lines he worked through on his own.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.tiffin.w: Invite Ishan and Deven to spend twenty minutes after dismissal solving one unseen problem together.
Both agree right away—twenty minutes after the bell beats five anxious minutes before morning register.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.tiffin.r: Keep your own notebook in your bag until the monitor collects the pile.
Mira Sen collects the row's notebooks on the bell, and everyone's submission stands on its own work.
strings.school_scene.p2.copied_homework.after_sc: In Room XI-A after the 15:50 bell, Ishan Sheikh and Deven Chakraborty open the textbook to the starred problem at the bottom of the page.
Take turns writing one line of the derivation each until the starred problem is solved.
By the time you wipe the board, Ishan can set up the equations without peeking at anyone's margin.
Tuck the returned hint card back into your folder and lock the classroom shutter.
Deven hands back the hint card without a crease, and the three of you walk out to the courtyard together.
Leave the textbook example for individual homework and head out on the bell.
Ishan thanks you for the earlier hint and packs his bag to catch the bus on time.
strings.school_scene.p2.load_shedding_night.titl: Load-Shedding on the Eve of the Test
strings.school_scene.p2.load_shedding_night.summ: A two-hour evening feeder cut is announced across the para on the night before a unit test, squeezing household chores, emergency lanterns and revision into the same window.
strings.school_scene.p2.load_shedding_night.warn: During sixth-period Bengali in the Class XI Science room, Ishan Sheikh mentions that the locality transformer by the lane corner has a scheduled 19:00–21:00 load-shedding cut tonight—right across the evening before tomorrow's unit test.
Plan to finish household water-bucket and kitchen chores before 19:00 so the lantern hour stays free for study.
You note the 19:00 cut window in your diary so you can coordinate with your household adult as soon as you reach home.
Speak with the care worker at handover about finishing pump and dining duties before the 19:00 cut.
You jot down the feeder cut hours to share at the care home desk before shift handover.
Keep your usual evening pace and hope the feeder comes back early.
Mira Sen wishes you luck with the evening revision as the dismissal bell rings.
strings.school_scene.p2.load_shedding_night.fami: Before the Feeder Trips at Home
At home at 18:15, the ceiling fan is still spinning while your household adult checks the rechargeable lantern and the kitchen water buckets before the 19:00 cut.
Fill the water buckets and finish your household turn now so 19:00–21:00 is clear at the lantern table.
When the street goes dark at 19:00 sharp, the chores are already done and the rechargeable lamp sits steady beside your notebook.
Split the evening chores and share the single bright lamp at the dining table for forty-five-minute turns.
Sharing the lamp table keeps the flat calm and gives you a focused hour for your hardest definitions.
Wait on the veranda for the power to return rather than working by the hot emergency lamp.
You rest your eyes in the veranda breeze until the streetlamps flicker back on at 20:50.
strings.school_scene.p2.load_shedding_night.care: Lantern Rota at the Care Home Desk
At the care home desk at 14:15, the care worker checks the battery charge on the two hall emergency lamps ahead of tonight's announced feeder cut.
Ask to finish your corridor and water-cooler rota before 18:30 so you can sit by the study lamp during the cut.
The care worker updates the evening clipboard so your duty wraps up before the transformer trips.
Arrange a shared four-student circle around the main common-room emergency lantern.
The care worker logs the shared lantern table in the handover book so everyone preparing for tomorrow's test gets light.
Keep your normal rota slot and do your reading before dusk instead.
The care worker nods and leaves your regular evening entry unchanged.
strings.school_scene.p2.load_shedding_night.revi: At 19:30 in the warm stillness of the outage, Ishan Sheikh quizzes you from the summary card in the white circle of the rechargeable lamp.
Make the early-dusk chore schedule your standing rule for every test-eve this term.
Finishing chores before dusk turns even a two-hour feeder cut into a quiet, unbroken revision block.
Keep the shared lantern quiz circle going until the neighbourhood fans hum back to life.
Testing each other aloud in the dim room makes the formulas stick better than silent reading ever did.
Pack your books away early once the lamp battery drops to one bar and get a full night's sleep.
You wake up fresh for the morning bell while half the section is yawning over their desks.
strings.school_scene.p2.wall_magazine_deadline.s: Two days before the Durga Puja vacation, Class XI's Bengali wall-magazine (*Prachir Patrika*) still needs its painted border, proofread columns and corridor mounting.
strings.school_scene.p2.wall_magazine_deadline.c: At the end of sixth-period Bengali in the Class XI Humanities room, Amrita Basu unrolls the half-finished Sharadiya wall-magazine board—two essay columns still need fair-copying and the alpana border is only pencilled in before the Puja holidays begin.
Divide the proofreading and border ruling with Mira Sen and Tara Das right away.
Mira takes the poem slips, Tara takes the wooden frame pins, and you take the central column layout.
Ask to bring the masthead strips home tonight so you can ink the Bengali lettering at your table.
Amrita Basu rolls the cartridge-paper masthead strips into a cardboard tube for you to check at home.
Ask to ink the masthead strips at the care home common-room table tonight.
You pack the pencilled masthead strips carefully to check the common-room table schedule this evening.
Wish the editorial team well and keep your pre-Puja afternoons clear for backlog catch-up.
Amrita Basu nods warmly and hands the remaining column to Deven Chakraborty without any pressure.
strings.school_scene.p2.wall_magazine_deadline.f: At home at 19:00, the smell of pre-Puja camphor drifts from the cupboard while your household adult watches you weight down the cartridge paper for the *Prachir Patrika* header.
Ink the Sharadiya masthead and alpana corner motifs cleanly before 20:00.
Your household adult steadies the steel ruler for the baseline, and the vermilion-and-black lettering dries crisp and straight.
Leave the masthead in pencil for tomorrow's tiffin break so your evening stays free.
You slide the uninked strips back into the tube and keep your evening unhurried.
strings.school_scene.p2.wall_magazine_deadline.c: Lettering the Header in the Common Room
In the care home study room at 19:00, the care worker admires the pencilled Bengali calligraphy on the *Prachir Patrika* masthead strip.
Spend forty minutes inking the masthead and border strips at the corner of the study table.
The care worker lends a clean blotter from the office desk, and the finished header looks ready for a printed journal.
Keep the study table clear for the younger residents and leave the inking for school hours.
You pack the strips safely back into the tube and spend a quiet evening over your books.
strings.school_scene.p2.wall_magazine_deadline.t: During tiffin break in the courtyard, Mira Sen lines up the handwritten poems and essays with a pot of gum while Deven Chakraborty checks the column margins.
Deliver your fair-copied column and return Mira's lettering pens before the bell.
Mira checks the alignment with a pleased nod and caps her pens with five minutes of tiffin still to spare.
Agree to stay after dismissal with Tara and Deven to mount and hang the finished board in the corridor.
Tara sets aside the brass picture hooks so the team can hang the board before the Puja holiday bell.
Hand in your drafted slip now and leave the afternoon mounting to the rest of the committee.
Deven and Mira thank you for the neat column and take over the paste-up from there.
strings.school_scene.p2.wall_magazine_deadline.h: Hanging the Sharadiya Board After Dismissal
In the courtyard corridor after the 15:50 bell, Tara Das steadies the wooden easel frame while Deven holds the spirit level against the wall hook.
Trim the final border corners together and lift the Sharadiya board onto the corridor hooks.
Amrita Basu stops by the corridor as the board settles level on the wall, reading the credits aloud with genuine pride.
Clean the brushes and return Mira's calligraphy set to her satchel before the gate closes.
Mira thanks you for returning every nib clean and dry as the Puja holidays begin.
Head out once the paste-up is dry and leave the corridor hanging to Tara and Deven.
Tara waves from the corridor step and promises you first look at the mounted board tomorrow morning.
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.title: The Primary-Lane Walk Home
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.summar: Drainage repairs along the para lane force the primary section's dismissal route onto the main road, creating a mid-afternoon escort obligation for a younger child.
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.messag: A Note About the Primary-Section Lane

During fifth-period Sociology in the Class XI Humanities room, word comes round that municipal drainage trenches have closed the narrow footpath outside the primary wing; younger children walking toward Nabapara must now cross the busier main road at dismissal.
Plan to talk with your household adult tonight about walking your younger cousin and neighbour home after the bell.
Tara Das notes that her own brother uses the same crossing, and you jot down the dismissal timings to check at home.
Plan to speak with the care worker at handover about escorting the two Class IV care-home juniors past the roadworks.
You note the road-repair diversion in your diary to discuss at the care home desk before 15:00.
Keep your own dismissal walk unchanged and leave the primary crossing to the gate staff.
Tara nods without complaint and checks the gate guard's crossing schedule after class.
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.family: Adjusting the Afternoon Walk at Home
At home at 18:20, your household adult looks worriedly at the municipal notice about the dug-up lane between the primary gate and your turn.
Combine the primary-gate pickup with your afternoon bread-and-milk errand right at 15:55.
Walking the younger child home along the errand route clears both tasks by 16:30 and leaves your evening revision untouched.
Alternate the afternoon crossing days with Tara Das so each of you walks three days a week.
Your household adult welcomes the shared roster with Tara, cutting the detour in half for both families.
Leave the primary-gate walk to the adults so you can come straight home to study.
Your household adult arranges to adjust their own afternoon hour until the lane paving is finished.
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.care.t: Coordinating the Junior Escort at Handover
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.care.p: At the care home desk at 14:20, the care worker checks the return timings for the two Class IV residents who walk back along the trenched lane.
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.care.r: Pair the afternoon primary-gate escort with your post-school sign-in so your evening rota starts thirty minutes later.
The care worker logs the paired walk in the handover book and credits the escort toward your afternoon house duty.
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.care.s: Set up an alternating escort roster with Tara Das and another senior resident along the same lane.
The care worker pins the alternating three-day roster to the noticeboard so no senior loses their whole week of free afternoons.
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.care.r: Keep your direct post-bell return and let the afternoon staff handle the primary crossing.
The care worker notes your unit-test workload and assigns a staff escort for the main-road stretch.
strings.school_scene.p2.sibling_walk_home.settle: Checking the Afternoon Route in the Evening
At 19:30 during evening study, Mira Sen passes over the updated neighbourhood map while you review how the afternoon walk held up.
Confirm the combined dismissal-and-errand walk with Amrita Basu and your household for the rest of the roadworks.
Folding the walk into the 15:55 errand keeps the younger children safe across the main road and protects your 18:30 study block.
Confirm the alternating weekday walking roster with Tara Das.
Sharing the crossing days with Tara turns a stressful detour into a steady fifteen-minute walk three times a week.
Step back from the standing escort arrangement once the first week's diversion signs are up.
Mira and Tara adjust the walking pair without hard feelings, leaving your afternoons open.
strings.school_scene.p2.friend_moving_away.title: Crates by the Stairwell
strings.school_scene.p2.friend_moving_away.summa: Just after the January class test, news spreads that a close friend's household is shifting out of the lane, leaving a few short afternoons to help with book crates and transfer records.
strings.school_scene.p2.friend_moving_away.tiffi: A Transfer Slip Mentioned at Tiffin

During tiffin break in the courtyard, Ishan Sheikh stares quietly at a twine-tied bundle of past question papers before admitting that his uncle's landlord is reclaiming their ground-floor rooms—part of the household is shifting across the river after the January test, and he may have to change bus routes or sections.
Sit down beside Ishan and ask what needs sorting before the tempo van arrives on Saturday.
Ishan breathes out and admits that sorting six years of school books and getting his practical file attested in time has been keeping him awake.
Tell Ishan you will check at home tonight whether you can spare an hour after school to help bundle his book crates.
Ishan's face brightens as you promise to check your household schedule before committing.
Tell Ishan you will ask the care worker at handover for a forty-minute afternoon detour pass to help pack.
Ishan thanks you warmly as you plan to check the care home sign-out ledger first.
Offer a sympathetic word and leave him quiet space to finish his tiffin without prying.
Ishan appreciates that you do not make a fuss in front of the whole courtyard.
strings.school_scene.p2.friend_moving_away.famil: Clearing an Hour at Home for Packing
At home at 18:30, your household adult listens as you explain Ishan's household move and the stack of textbooks waiting to be tied in jute twine.
Finish tomorrow's household chores early so you can spend forty minutes after dismissal helping Ishan pack.
Your household adult hands you a roll of stout jute twine from the kitchen drawer to take along tomorrow.
Keep your post-school hours focused on January test revision at home.
Your household adult understands that January test week leaves very little margin for extra afternoon trips.
Logging a Farewell Detour at Handover
At the care home desk at 14:10, the care worker opens the afternoon return ledger while you explain that a classmate's household is shifting rooms this week.
Log a forty-minute post-dismissal detour in the handover book so you can help tie up the book crates.
The care worker signs the 16:30 return note and gives you two empty cardboard cartons from the storeroom to carry over.
Keep your standard post-bell return time in the care home ledger.
The care worker nods kindly and keeps your afternoon sign-in unchanged.
strings.school_scene.p2.friend_moving_away.engli: As fourth-period English ends in the Class XI Science room, Tara Das writes her landline and para landmark on the back of an index card for Ishan while he checks his practical record folder.
Promise to meet Ishan at the gate after last bell to cord the book bundles and carry them to the stand.
Ishan grins with relief—having two pairs of hands means the heavy reference volumes will not split the cartons.
Walk with Ishan to Amrita Basu's table to get his mid-year practical observations stamped and attested.
Amrita Basu stamps every practical page and confirms that his attendance register allows him to keep his seat at Nabapara even from the new bus route.
Write your address clearly in his notebook and wish his family a smooth move.
Ishan tucks your address card carefully into his geometry box and thanks you for the steady company all term.
Walking the Book Bundles Toward Shanti Chai Corner
Outside the school gate after the 15:50 bell, Ishan Sheikh balances two twine-tied bundles of Class XI books while Farida Qadri waves from Shanti Chai Corner down the lane toward the bus stand.
Carry the heavier bundle with him past Shanti Chai Corner to the Nabapara Bus Stand bench.
Farida Qadri sets out two small glasses of lemon cha as you set the crates down by the stand, and Ishan promises to save your seat on the morning bus from the new stop.
Bring Amrita Basu's signed attendance and bus-concession slip out to Ishan before his uncle's van arrives.
With the signed bus-concession form in hand, Ishan knows he can finish Class XI with the same section despite the longer commute.
Help him lift the crate at the school gate and head home before the afternoon traffic thickens.
Ishan claps your shoulder gratefully at the gate corner and heads down the lane toward the bus stand.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.title: The Canteen Chalkboard and the Tiffin Petition
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.summary: When the school canteen chalks up a sudden price rise on singaras and the basic lunch plate, students debate whether to circulate a petition, pool home tiffin tins, or stay out of the row.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.board.t: New Rates Chalked on the Canteen Board
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.board.p: At tiffin break in the courtyard, a small crowd gathers around the canteen shutter: the chalked rate for a singara-and-ghugni plate has jumped by five rupees overnight—more than Farida Qadri charges outside the lane—and Mira Sen is already ruling columns in her notebook to calculate what that adds across a month.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.board.t: Help Mira compare the old and new weekly tiffin costs so any representation uses exact figures.
Mira notes down the exact rupee difference for students who rely on the midday staple plate when morning classes run early.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.board.f: Check at home tonight whether you can pack an extra tiffin tin of muri and cucumber to share on the bench.
You make a note to check the kitchen tins at home this evening before signing anything.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.board.c: Check with the care worker at handover whether the care home kitchen can pack a larger shared tiffin tin.
You plan to speak with the care worker before 15:00 about the afternoon tiffin allocation.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.board.r: Step back from the canteen crowd and eat your own packed tiffin in peace.
You sit by the courtyard banyan shade with Ishan Sheikh while the debate around the chalkboard carries on.
Packing a Shared Tiffin Tin at Home
At home at 18:30, your household adult shakes their head at the new canteen rates while measuring out puffed rice and roasted peanuts into the steel tiffin carrier.
Pack the two-tier steel tiffin box tomorrow so classmates short on change do not go hungry at break.
Your household adult adds chopped chillies, cucumber and mustard oil in the small lid compartment so there is plenty to pass around.
Keep your usual single tiffin box and leave the canteen dispute to the school committee.
Your household adult packs your standard tiffin tin and advises you to stay polite if the petition comes round.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.care.ti: Asking About the Tiffin Tin at Handover
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.care.pr: At the care home desk at 14:15, the care worker listens as you mention the five-rupee rise on the school canteen's midday plate.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.care.pa: Ask to sign out the larger steel tiffin carrier from the pantry so the care-home students can share at break.
The care worker writes a kitchen slip for an extra portion of spiced chana and muri in the shared carrier.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.care.re: Keep your individual tiffin packet as usual without changing the kitchen order.
The care worker notes the canteen price rise in the house logbook and leaves your daily packet unchanged.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.draft.t: The Petition Sheet Before Third-Period Economics
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.draft.p: In the Class XI Commerce room before third-period Economics, Mira Sen and Tara Das look over two drafts: an angry boycott sheet from the back bench, and a factual request asking the school to keep one basic plate at the old rate.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.draft.s: Set up a shared courtyard tiffin circle with Tara so nobody has to buy the overpriced plate this week.
Tara organises five steel tins along the courtyard bench, taking the immediate pressure off classmates on a tight daily allowance.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.draft.a: Take Mira's factual cost sheet to Amrita Basu and ask her to place it before the school welfare committee.
Amrita Basu commends the calm, arithmetic-backed note and agrees to carry it to the headmaster's canteen review.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.draft.r: Decline to sign either sheet so your name stays off the petition list.
Mira respects your choice without pressing you, and passes the clipboard to the next bench.
strings.school_scene.p2.canteen_petition.committ: In the courtyard after the 15:50 dismissal bell, Tara Das and Ishan Sheikh wait by the canteen noticeboard as the contractor wipes the bottom line of the slate.
Keep the courtyard shared-tiffin bench running every Tuesday and Thursday regardless of the board price.
The shared muri-and-fruit circle becomes a favourite tiffin habit across all three streams.
Thank Amrita Basu as the school confirms that the plain ghugni-and-bread student plate stays at the old tariff.
Amrita Basu notes that Mira's clean cost table did more work than ten pages of shouting ever could.
Head out at the bell and leave the canteen committee follow-up to Mira and Tara.
Ishan walks with you toward the gate as the afternoon crowd thins out.
strings.school_scene.p2.lost_library_book.title: The Reference Volume on the Morning Bus
strings.school_scene.p2.lost_library_book.summar: A stamped school library reference book slips out of your satchel on the crowded morning bus to Nabapara Bus Stand just days before the half-yearly library clearance.
strings.school_scene.p2.lost_library_book.tiffin: An Empty Slot in the Satchel

During tiffin break in the courtyard, you reach into your satchel for the purple-stamped school library copy of *Selected Essays & précis Passages*—and feel only your geometry box; the book must have slipped onto the seat of the crowded 09:45 bus before Nabapara Bus Stand.
Ask Ishan Sheikh right away which conductor and bus number run the 09:45 turn through Nabapara Bus Stand.
Ishan flips open his pocket notebook: he knows the afternoon return timing for that exact route and offers to check the starter's kiosk with you.
Plan to tell your household adult tonight and check the secondhand bookstalls if the bus search fails.
You copy down the library accession number from your issue card so you can explain the loss honestly at home.
Plan to tell the care worker at handover and ask for a gate pass to check the bus stand lost-property shelf.
You note the accession number and bus route in your diary to bring to the care home desk before 15:00.
Say nothing for now and re-check the classroom benches on your own.
You search beneath the desks in silence before the bell, hoping the volume turns up in the room.
strings.school_scene.p2.lost_library_book.family: Owning Up About the Library Book at Home
At home at 18:30, you place the buff library borrower's card on the table and explain to your household adult how the book slipped off the bus bench.
Agree to check the bus stand starter's kiosk first and, if needed, hunt for an identical replacement edition together.
Your household adult is glad you spoke up immediately rather than letting overdue fines pile up before the half-yearly clearance.
Hold off on asking for replacement money until you have checked the school corridor one more day.
You tuck the borrower's card back into your diary and resolve to check the school office yourself tomorrow.
strings.school_scene.p2.lost_library_book.care.t: Reporting the Missing Volume at Handover
strings.school_scene.p2.lost_library_book.care.p: At the care home desk at 14:10, the care worker looks at your school library card as you explain the morning bus mix-up.
strings.school_scene.p2.lost_library_book.care.a: Request a thirty-minute post-dismissal pass to visit the Nabapara Bus Stand starter's booth with Ishan.
The care worker signs the pass and writes the school's stamp description on a slip for the bus starter.
strings.school_scene.p2.lost_library_book.care.r: Keep the matter to yourself for another day before logging an official loss note.
The care worker finishes the afternoon handover calmly while you keep the library card in your pocket.
strings.school_scene.p2.lost_library_book.ledger: Checking the Accession Details Before First Period

At the start of first-period Accountancy in the Class XI Commerce room, Mira Sen checks her own library slip—she borrowed the companion volume last month and remembers the exact publisher and binding colour.
Arrange with Ishan to meet at the gate at 15:55 to catch the same bus crew on their afternoon loop.
Mira writes the publisher's imprint and purple stamp mark on a card so the bus conductor can recognise it immediately.
Go straight to Amrita Basu to report the missing volume and ask for a one-week grace period before fines start.
Amrita Basu notes your prompt honesty in the library register and grants a seven-day renewal window to find or replace the book.
Thank Mira for the publisher details and handle the library counter quietly on your own.
Mira slips the publisher note into your hand and wishes you luck before the register is called.
